summary: Al-Fatiha means 'The Opening.' It is the first surah in the Quran. We say it in every prayer. In it we thank Allah and say that we worship only Him. Then we ask Allah to show us the right way.
questions: Why do we ask Allah to show us the right way every day?
What do you want to thank Allah for today?
What is one thing you can do to follow the right way this week?

summary: Al-Baqarah means 'The Cow.' It is the longest surah. It tells the story of Adam and the story of Musa. It has the story of a cow, so it got this name. It teaches rules for life, like fasting, giving, and being honest. It has Ayat al-Kursi, a very great verse.
questions: Which rule in this surah is hard for you? Why?
How does Ayat al-Kursi show that Allah is always with you?
What is one kind thing you can give to someone this week?

summary: This surah is named after the family of Imran. It tells about Maryam, Zakariya and Isa. Isa was a prophet and a servant of Allah. It also tells about the Battle of Uhud. Some people did not listen to the Prophet, and the Muslims lost. We learn to be patient, stay together and trust Allah.
questions: What can we learn from the mistake at Uhud?
Why is it good to stay together?
How can you be patient when something is hard?

summary: An-Nisa means 'The Women.' It teaches us to treat women, families and children with no parents in a fair and kind way. It tells us how to share money and things in a fair way. It says to always be fair, even when it is hard.
questions: Why should we take care of children who have no parents?
When is it hard for you to be fair?
How can you help someone in your family today?

summary: Al-Ma'idah means 'The Table.' It starts with: 'Keep your promises.' It tells us which foods are okay to eat. It says to be fair, even to people you do not like. It tells about two sons of Adam. One was jealous and hurt his brother. That was very wrong. It also tells how the friends of Isa asked for a table of food from the sky.
questions: Why is it important to keep a promise?
What can being jealous do to a heart?
How can you be fair to a person you do not like?

summary: Al-An'am means 'The Cattle.' It teaches that only Allah made everything. It shows the sky, plants and animals as signs of Allah. It tells how Ibrahim looked at a star, the moon and the sun. He knew that only the One who made them should be worshipped. It tells us to be honest and kind.
questions: What sign of Allah do you love to see?
What did Ibrahim learn when he looked at the stars and the moon?
How can you be more honest today?

summary: Al-A'raf means 'The High Places.' It tells about Adam and Iblis, who is Shaytan. It tells about the prophets Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut, Shu'ayb and Musa. They told their people to follow Allah. The people who said no were punished. We learn that Shaytan is our enemy, and that we should listen to the prophets.
questions: Why did Iblis say no to Allah?
How can you stay away from Shaytan?
Which prophet's story do you like best?

summary: Al-Anfal is about the Battle of Badr. A small group of believers won against a very big army, because Allah helped them. This surah teaches us to trust Allah, to stay together and not to fight each other.
questions: How did Allah help the believers at Badr?
Why is fighting with each other bad for a group?
When did you feel that Allah helped you?

summary: At-Tawbah means 'Saying Sorry to Allah.' It is the only surah that does not start with Bismillah. It tells about a long, hard trip to Tabuk in the hot weather. It tells about people who only pretended to believe. It also tells about believers who made mistakes, said sorry, and Allah forgave them.
questions: How do we say sorry to Allah?
What is the difference between pretending and really believing?
Is there something you want to say sorry to Allah for?

summary: Yunus is named after Prophet Yunus (Jonah). His people believed in time, and Allah saved them. This surah also tells about Musa and Pharaoh. Pharaoh said he believed only when he was drowning. That was too late. We should turn to Allah before it is too late.
questions: Why should we turn to Allah early?
How is the Quran like medicine for the heart?
How can you show that you are happy with Allah's kindness?

summary: Hud is named after Prophet Hud. It tells the stories of Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Lut, Shu'ayb and Musa. Many people did not listen to their prophet, and they were destroyed. Allah tells the Prophet to stay strong and to keep doing what is right.
questions: What helped the prophets stay strong when people said no?
How can you stay strong when others do wrong?
Why is it good to keep doing the right thing?

summary: Yusuf tells the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph). When he was a boy, he had a dream. His brothers were jealous and threw him in a well. He was taken to Egypt, and he was put in jail for something he did not do. Later he became a leader in Egypt. He forgave his brothers and saw his father again. Allah calls it the best of stories.
questions: How was Yusuf patient?
Why did Yusuf forgive his brothers?
What does this story teach you about trusting Allah?

summary: Ar-Ra'd means 'The Thunder.' It shows thunder, lightning and rain as signs of Allah. Even the thunder praises Allah. It says that hearts feel calm when we remember Allah. Truth stays, like water. Bad things go away, like foam.
questions: When does your heart feel calm?
What can foam and water teach us about the truth?
How can you remember Allah more during the day?

summary: Ibrahim is named after Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham). It has his beautiful duas. He asked Allah to keep Makkah safe and to help his children pray. It says: if you say thank you, Allah gives you more. The prophets take people out of the dark and into the light.
questions: What is one gift you can thank Allah for right now?
What do Ibrahim's duas for his children teach us?
What does it mean to go from the dark into the light?

summary: Al-Hijr is the name of a place with homes cut in rocks. In this surah Allah promises to keep the Quran safe. It tells how Iblis would not bow to Adam. It tells about the angels who visited Ibrahim, and about the people of Lut. Allah tells the Prophet to be patient and to forgive in a nice way.
questions: How do you feel that Allah keeps the Quran safe?
What does it look like to forgive in a nice way?
How can being proud stop a person from doing right?

summary: An-Nahl means 'The Bee.' It lists many gifts from Allah: rain, plants, animals, the sea and the bee that makes honey. It teaches us to say thank you, to be fair and kind, and to keep our promises. It says to invite people to Allah with wise and kind words.
questions: Which gift of Allah do you forget to thank Him for?
What can a little bee teach us?
How can you invite someone to good with kind words?

summary: Al-Isra means 'The Night Trip.' It starts with the night when Allah took the Prophet from Makkah to Jerusalem. It teaches good manners: be kind to your parents, do not waste things, keep your promises, be honest, and do not be proud.
questions: Why does Allah tell us to be kind to our parents?
How can you waste less?
Which good manner do you want to work on most?

summary: Al-Kahf means 'The Cave.' It has four stories. One is about young men who hid in a cave to keep their faith. One is about a man with two gardens. One is about Musa and Khidr. One is about a strong king named Dhul-Qarnayn. They teach us about tests with faith, money, knowledge and power. Many Muslims read this surah on Friday.
questions: Which test is the hardest for you: faith, money, knowledge or power?
What did Musa learn from Khidr?
Why do you think we read this surah on Friday?

summary: Maryam is named after Maryam (Mary), the mother of Isa. It tells how Allah gave Zakariya a son named Yahya, and how Isa was born. Isa spoke when he was a baby. He said he was a servant of Allah. Nothing is too hard for Allah. Allah is Ar-Rahman, the Most Kind.
questions: What can we learn from Zakariya's dua?
How did Maryam trust Allah in a hard time?
What does it mean to you that nothing is too hard for Allah?

summary: This surah tells the story of Musa. He saw a fire on a mountain. Allah talked to him. His stick turned into a snake. He went to Pharaoh with his brother Harun. It also tells how Shaytan tricked Adam. Allah says the Quran was not sent to make life hard. It is a reminder.
questions: What dua did Musa say before he went to Pharaoh?
Why is the Quran not a heavy load?
How did the magicians change when they saw the truth?

summary: Al-Anbiya means 'The Prophets.' It tells about many prophets: Ibrahim, Nuh, Dawud, Sulayman, Ayyub, Yunus and Zakariya. Allah helped each one. All of them had one message: worship Allah alone. It reminds people that the Day of Judgment is near.
questions: What did all the prophets have in common?
Which prophet's dua would you like to remember?
Why do people forget about the Last Day?

summary: Al-Hajj means 'The Trip to Makkah.' Ibrahim built the Kaaba and called people to Hajj. It tells how scary the Last Day will be. It says people who were treated badly may defend themselves. It ends by telling us to bow down, worship Allah and do good.
questions: Why do all Muslims wear the same clothes at Hajj?
How can you do good for Allah this week?
How can you get your heart ready for the Last Day?

summary: Al-Mu'minun means 'The Believers.' It starts with: 'The believers have won.' Believers are calm in prayer, stay away from useless talk, give to people in need, and keep their promises. It tells how a person grows before birth. It tells about Nuh and other prophets. It ends with a dua to ask Allah to forgive us.
questions: Which thing about the believers do you want to have?
What does it mean to be calm in prayer?
How can you stay away from useless talk?

summary: An-Nur means 'The Light.' It has rules to keep families safe, like being modest and asking before you go into a house. It tells how some people told a lie about Aisha, and Allah showed that she was telling the truth. It teaches us not to spread rumors. It says Allah is the Light of the sky and the earth.
questions: Why is it bad to spread rumors?
How can you protect another person's good name?
What does it mean that Allah is the Light of the sky and the earth?

summary: Al-Furqan means 'The One That Tells Right From Wrong.' This is the Quran. It tells how people laughed at the Prophet. It ends by telling about the servants of the Most Kind. They walk gently, answer rude people with 'Peace,' pray at night, and do not waste.
questions: How does the Quran help you tell right from wrong?
How can you answer a rude person with 'Peace'?
Which thing about the servants of the Most Kind do you want most?

summary: Ash-Shu'ara means 'The Poets.' It tells the stories of Musa, Ibrahim, Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb. After each story it says that this is a sign, but most people did not believe. These stories cheer up the Prophet when people said no. The truth wins in the end.
questions: Why do you think the same words come after each story?
What do these stories teach about being patient?
How does it feel to know that Allah is strong and also kind?

summary: An-Naml means 'The Ant.' Prophet Sulayman could understand animals. An ant told the other ants to go inside. Sulayman smiled and thanked Allah. A bird called the hoopoe told him about a queen named Bilqis. She worshipped the sun, but later she believed in Allah. We learn to be thankful and not proud.
questions: What did Sulayman do when Allah gave him so much?
What can the little ant teach us?
How can you say thank you to Allah for what He gave you?

summary: Al-Qasas means 'The Stories.' It tells the story of Musa from when he was a baby. His mother put him in the river to keep him safe. He grew up in Pharaoh's house. Later he became a prophet. It also tells about Qarun, a rich man who was proud. The earth swallowed him. Being proud is bad.
questions: How did Allah take care of baby Musa?
What mistake did Qarun make with his money?
How can you stay humble when you have something good?

summary: Al-Ankabut means 'The Spider.' It says Allah tests believers to show who is real. Nuh called his people for 950 years. A spider's house is the weakest house. People who trust anyone but Allah are like that. We should be patient and ask Allah for help.
questions: Why does Allah test believers?
What does the spider's house teach us?
What hard thing are you going through, and how can you be patient?

summary: Ar-Rum means 'The Romans.' It says the Romans, who had lost a war, would win in a few years. This came true. It shows signs of Allah: people made from dust, husbands and wives with love between them, different languages and colors, sleep, and rain. Allah's promise is true.
questions: Which sign of Allah in this surah makes you think the most?
What does it mean that Allah put love between husbands and wives?
How does the story of the Romans show that Allah's promise is true?

summary: Luqman was a wise man. He gave advice to his son. He said: Do not worship anyone but Allah. Be good to your parents. Even a very small good thing is counted. Pray. Tell people to do good. Be patient. Do not be proud. Keep your voice low.
questions: Which advice of Luqman helps you the most today?
What does it mean that even a tiny good thing is counted?
Why did Luqman tell his son to keep his voice low?

summary: As-Sajdah means 'The Bowing Down.' It tells how Allah made the sky and the earth in six days and made people from clay. It tells about believers who wake up at night to pray. No one knows the happy things Allah hid for them in Paradise.
questions: Why is praying at night so special?
What do you think Allah hid for the believers in Paradise?
How can you make dua at night?

summary: Al-Ahzab means 'The Armies.' It tells about the Battle of the Trench. Many groups came to attack Madinah. The Muslims dug a trench and were patient. Allah sent a strong wind and the armies went away. It says the Prophet is the best example for us. It also teaches about family and modest dress.
questions: What helped the believers stay strong at the Battle of the Trench?
How is the Prophet the best example for you?
How can you trust Allah when you are scared?

summary: Saba is the name of a place. This surah tells about Dawud and Sulayman, who were given great gifts. The people of Saba lived in beautiful gardens, but they did not say thank you. A flood came and destroyed their dam. We should be thankful for what we have.
questions: What did the people of Saba lose? Why?
How can you show thanks, and not only say it?
What gift do you have that can help other people?

summary: Fatir means 'The Maker.' Allah made the sky and the earth. He made angels with wings. Rain, mountains and the many colors in nature are signs. People who know about Allah fear Him the most. Shaytan is our enemy. No one will carry the load of another person.
questions: Why do people who know more fear Allah more?
What does it mean that no one carries another person's load?
How can you treat Shaytan as an enemy?

summary: Ya-Sin is called the heart of the Quran. It tells about a town where messengers came. A man ran from the end of the city to tell people to follow them. It shows signs of Allah, like dead land coming alive after rain, the night and day, and the sun and moon. When Allah wants something, He says 'Be' and it is.
questions: Why did the man run from the end of the city?
Which sign of Allah in this surah amazes you most?
What does it mean that Allah just says 'Be' and it is?

summary: As-Saffat means 'Those Standing in Rows.' It starts with angels standing in rows. It tells how Ibrahim broke the idols. It tells how Ibrahim was ready to give his son for Allah. Allah saved the boy and gave a big sheep instead. It also tells about Nuh, Musa, Harun, Ilyas, Lut and Yunus.
questions: What does Ibrahim's story teach us about listening to Allah?
What did Yunus say when he was inside the big fish?
What does it mean to give yourself fully to Allah?

summary: Sad is a letter of the Arabic alphabet. This surah tells about Prophets Dawud, Sulayman and Ayyub (Job). Ayyub was very sick and lost many things. He was patient and Allah made him well. It also tells how Iblis was too proud to bow to Adam.
questions: What can you learn from Ayyub being patient?
Why did being proud get Iblis thrown out?
When you make a mistake, how do you go back to Allah?

summary: Az-Zumar means 'The Groups.' It says to worship Allah with an honest heart. It has a very kind verse: 'Do not lose hope in Allah's kindness. Allah forgives all sins.' It tells how people will go in groups on the Last Day, some to Hell and some to Paradise.
questions: What does it mean to worship Allah with an honest heart?
Why should we never lose hope in Allah?
What would you tell a friend who thinks Allah cannot forgive him?

summary: Ghafir means 'The One Who Forgives.' Allah forgives sins and accepts us when we say sorry. It tells about a man in Pharaoh's family who hid his faith and then spoke up for Musa. Allah says: 'Call on Me and I will answer you.'
questions: What does it mean to you that Allah says 'Call on Me and I will answer'?
What made the man in Pharaoh's family so brave?
How can you make dua more often?

summary: Fussilat means 'Made Clear.' It says the Quran is made clear. It tells about Ad and Thamud. On the Last Day, ears, eyes and skin will tell what we did. It teaches: answer bad with good, and an enemy can become like a close friend.
questions: Think of a time when someone was rude to you. How could you answer with something good?
What does it mean that our body will tell what we did?
Why is it hard to answer bad with good?

summary: Ash-Shura means 'Talking It Over.' Believers talk together and ask for advice before they decide. All the prophets came with one message. It teaches us to forgive. Whoever forgives and makes peace gets a reward from Allah.
questions: Why is it good to ask others for advice?
How does forgiving help your own heart?
How can you make peace when people are upset?

summary: Az-Zukhruf means 'Gold.' Some people thought that gold and money make a person great. Allah says this life is only a small thing. The next life is for people who fear and respect Allah. It tells about Ibrahim and Isa. On that Day, close friends will turn into enemies, except those who obeyed Allah.
questions: Does having more things make a person better? Why or why not?
What makes a friendship last into the next life?
How can you remember that this life is short?

summary: Ad-Dukhan means 'The Smoke.' It says Allah sent down the Quran on a blessed night. It tells how Pharaoh's people left behind gardens and nice houses. It warns about the Last Day. It says Paradise is for people who obey Allah.
questions: What did Pharaoh's people have to leave behind?
What will you want to take with you to the next life?
What do you think the blessed night is?

summary: Al-Jathiyah means 'Kneeling.' It shows signs of Allah in the sky, the earth, night and day, and rain. It says not to follow your own wants like they are your god. On the Last Day, every group will kneel and be called to see what they did.
questions: What does it mean to make your wants your god?
Which sign of Allah do you see most often?
How can you tell if you are following Allah or only what you want?

summary: Al-Ahqaf is the name of a sandy place. The people of Ad lived there. A strong wind destroyed them. It teaches us to be kind to our parents. It has a dua for a person who is forty years old: 'Help me to say thank you.' A group of jinn listened to the Quran and went back to tell their people.
questions: Why does Allah talk about parents so much in the Quran?
What would you ask Allah to help you with when you are forty?
What can we learn from the jinn who listened and then told others?

summary: This surah is named after Prophet Muhammad. It tells believers to obey Allah and His Messenger. If you help Allah's way, Allah will help you and keep your feet firm. It asks: 'Do they not think about the Quran? Or are their hearts locked?' Allah has everything. We are the ones who need Him.
questions: How can you help Allah's way every day?
What can you do to think more about the Quran?
How does it feel to know that Allah has everything and you need Him?

summary: Al-Fath means 'The Win.' It came after the agreement at Hudaybiyyah. It looked like a loss, but it was a clear win. The believers made a promise to the Prophet under a tree. Allah put calm in their hearts. The Prophet's friends were strong, kind to each other, and always bowing to Allah.
questions: Why did the agreement look like a loss but turn out to be a win?
What does it mean to have calm in your heart?
Which thing about the Prophet's friends do you want to have?

summary: Al-Hujurat means 'The Rooms.' It teaches good manners. Do not speak loudly near the Prophet. Check the news before you believe it. Make peace between people who fight. Do not make fun of others. Do not talk about people behind their backs. Allah made us into different groups so we can know each other. The best person is the one who obeys Allah most.
questions: Why should we check news before we believe it?
What is the worst thing about talking behind someone's back?
What makes a person the best in Allah's eyes?

summary: Qaf is a letter of the Arabic alphabet. This surah is about coming back to life. Allah is closer to you than the vein in your neck. Two angels write down everything you say. Dead land comes alive after rain. This is a sign that Allah can bring us back to life.
questions: How do you feel knowing that two angels write down what you say?
What does it mean that Allah is closer than the vein in your neck?
What good word do you want to say more often?

summary: Adh-Dhariyat means 'The Winds That Scatter.' It tells about the angels who visited Ibrahim and gave him good news of a son. It also tells about Lut, Pharaoh, Ad, Thamud and Nuh. Allah says: 'I made jinn and people only to worship Me.'
questions: How can you worship Allah in daily life, not only in prayer?
How did Ibrahim show good manners to his guests?
What can you turn into worship today?

summary: At-Tur means 'The Mountain.' It is the mountain where Allah spoke to Musa. The surah says the Last Day is sure to come. People in Paradise will be happy with their families. It tells the Prophet to be patient and to praise Allah when he wakes up and at night.
questions: What does it mean to be patient with what Allah decides?
When do you praise Allah during the day?
How can your family be together in Paradise?

summary: An-Najm means 'The Star.' It tells how the Prophet saw Jibril. He went up to a very special tree. The Prophet does not speak from his own wants. Idols are just names. No one carries another person's load. You get what you work for. The surah ends by telling us to bow down.
questions: What does it mean that you get what you work for?
Why are idols just names?
How can you bow to Allah with a humble heart today?

summary: Al-Qamar means 'The Moon.' The moon split in two as a sign, but people said it was magic. It tells how Nuh's people, Ad, Thamud, Lut's people and Pharaoh were destroyed. It says again and again: 'We made the Quran easy to remember. Will anyone remember?'
questions: What does it mean that the Quran is easy to remember?
Why do some people still not believe when they see a sign?
What can you do this week to learn a little more Quran?

summary: Ar-Rahman means 'The Most Kind.' Allah taught the Quran, made people, and taught them to speak. He made the sun and the moon move in their paths. It asks again and again: 'Which of your Lord's gifts will you say no to?' It tells about two gardens in Paradise.
questions: Which gift of Allah in this surah do you notice most?
Why does Allah ask the same question so many times?
What gift of Allah have you forgotten to thank Him for?

summary: Al-Waqi'ah means 'The Event That Will Happen.' It is about the Last Day. People will be in three groups. The first group is closest to Allah. The second group is on the right. The third group is on the left. It tells about Paradise and Hell. It asks us to look at the seed we plant and the water we drink.
questions: Which group do you want to be in? What can you do to get there?
What does it mean that Allah is the One who grows the seed?
Why is the Quran so special?

summary: Al-Hadid means 'The Iron.' Everything in the sky and the earth praises Allah. It tells us to give in Allah's way. It says this life is like a game and a show. We should run to get Allah's forgiveness. Allah sent iron, which is strong and useful. Allah is with you wherever you are.
questions: What does it mean that this life is like a game and a show?
How can you give in Allah's way even if you have little?
How does it change you to know Allah is with you everywhere?

summary: Al-Mujadila means 'The Woman Who Argued.' A woman named Khawla came to the Prophet with a problem about her husband. Allah heard her and sent down these verses. It teaches good manners: make room for others. Do not whisper secrets to hurt people.
questions: What does it mean that Allah hears even a quiet complaint?
How can you make room for others at home or at school?
Why are secret whispers bad for a group?

summary: Al-Hashr means 'The Gathering.' It tells how one tribe in Madinah broke a promise and had to leave. It praises the helpers of Madinah, called the Ansar. They gave to others even when they needed things themselves. At the end are many beautiful names of Allah.
questions: What does it mean to give others what you need yourself?
Which beautiful name of Allah at the end do you like most?
How can you be a helper to someone today?

summary: Al-Mumtahanah means 'The Woman Who Is Tested.' It says do not make friends with people who fight against you for your faith. But Allah does not stop you from being kind and fair to people who do not hurt you. Ibrahim is an example of someone who stayed strong.
questions: How can you be kind and fair to people who believe differently?
What does it mean to stay strong like Ibrahim?
Why is being fair important, even to people you disagree with?

summary: As-Saff means 'The Lines.' It asks: 'Why do you say what you do not do?' Allah loves people who stand together like a strong wall. Isa told good news about a prophet who will come after him, named Ahmad. It tells us to be helpers of Allah.
questions: Is there something you say you will do but do not? How can you change?
What does it mean to stand together like a strong wall?
How can you be a helper of Allah today?

summary: Al-Jumu'ah means 'Friday.' When you hear the call for Friday prayer, hurry to remember Allah and stop your work. After the prayer, you can go back to work and look for Allah's gifts. It tells about people who had a book but did not follow it. They are like a donkey carrying books.
questions: Why does Allah tell us to stop our work for Friday prayer?
What does it mean to carry a book but not follow it?
How can you make Friday more special?

summary: Al-Munafiqun means 'Those Who Pretend.' These are people who say they believe but do not believe in their hearts. They look nice and talk well, but they are like wood leaning on a wall. Allah says: 'Do not let your money or your children make you forget Allah.'
questions: How can you make sure your words and your heart match?
What makes you forget Allah the most?
What good thing do you want to do before it is too late?

summary: At-Taghabun means 'Winning and Losing.' Everything praises Allah. Our family can be a test for us. Obey Allah as much as you can. Give to others. The one who does not let greed win is a winner.
questions: How can family be a gift and also a test?
What does it mean to not let greed win?
What does 'as much as you can' tell you about Allah?

summary: At-Talaq means 'Divorce.' It gives rules to be fair when a husband and wife part. It says: 'Whoever fears and respects Allah, Allah will make a way out for them. Allah will give them what they need from places they do not expect.'
questions: Why does Allah want us to be fair even in hard times?
What does it mean that Allah makes a way out for you?
When did Allah give you something from a place you did not expect?

summary: At-Tahrim means 'Saying No to Something.' It is about the Prophet's home and being honest in the family. It tells believers to say a real sorry to Allah. It gives good examples: Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh, and Maryam. Your faith belongs to you.
questions: What does a real sorry to Allah look like?
What can you learn from Asiya, who kept her faith in Pharaoh's house?
How can you keep yourself and your family safe from harm?

summary: Al-Mulk means 'The Kingdom.' Allah owns everything. He made life and death to see who does the best deeds. Look up at the sky. You will not see any mistake in it. Look at the birds with their wings open. Who can give you food if Allah stops? Many Muslims read this surah at night.
questions: Why did Allah make life and death?
What perfect thing in nature makes you think of Allah?
How can you remember that all your food and things come from Allah?

summary: Al-Qalam means 'The Pen.' Allah swears by the pen. He tells the Prophet that his character is great. It tells about the owners of a garden who forgot to say 'if Allah wills,' and lost everything. It tells the Prophet to be patient and not like Yunus when he was upset.
questions: Why should we say 'if Allah wills' when we make plans?
What makes a person's character great?
What does the garden story teach us about being greedy?

summary: Al-Haqqah means 'The Sure Thing.' It is about the Last Day. It tells what happened to Thamud, Ad and Pharaoh. On that Day some people will get their book in the right hand and be happy. Others will get it in the left hand and be sorry. The Quran is true.
questions: How do you feel when you think about getting your book on that Day?
What can you do each day to fill your book with good things?
Why does Allah tell us about people who were destroyed?

summary: Al-Ma'arij means 'The Stairs.' People are often worried and in a hurry. They complain when something bad happens, and they hold back when they have good things. But those who pray, give to the poor, believe in the Last Day, and keep their promises are not like that. Be patient in a beautiful way.
questions: When do you feel the most worried? What can you do?
Which quality of the saved people do you want most?
What does a beautiful patience look like?

summary: Nuh is named after Prophet Nuh (Noah). He called his people day and night. He told them to say sorry to Allah so Allah would send rain and give them money, children and gardens. They put their fingers in their ears. A great flood came. Nuh asked Allah to forgive him, his parents and the believers.
questions: What can we learn from Nuh being patient for so long?
What does saying sorry to Allah bring, according to this surah?
What dua do you want to make for your parents?

summary: Al-Jinn is about some jinn who listened to the Quran. They said: 'We heard an amazing Quran. It shows the right way. We believe in it.' Only Allah knows what we cannot see. The mosques belong to Allah, so call only on Him.
questions: What did the jinn like about the Quran?
What does it mean that only Allah knows what we cannot see?
How can you show respect for the mosque?

summary: Al-Muzzammil means 'The One Wrapped Up.' Allah told the Prophet to get up and pray at night. He told him to read the Quran slowly and clearly. Night is a quiet time to think. Be patient. Take Allah as your protector. Pray, give, and ask for forgiveness.
questions: Why is it good to read the Quran slowly and clearly?
What is a quiet time in your day when you can think about Allah?
What does it mean to take Allah as your protector?

summary: Al-Muddaththir means 'The One in a Cloak.' Allah told the Prophet: 'Get up and warn people. Say your Lord is greatest. Keep yourself clean. Stay away from bad things. Be patient for your Lord.' Every person is responsible for what they did.
questions: What does it mean to keep yourself clean inside and outside?
Why should we give without wanting something back?
What can you be patient about for Allah's sake?

summary: Al-Qiyamah means 'The Day People Get Up Again.' Allah swears by this day. People think Allah cannot put their bones back together. But He can even make their fingertips again. Some faces will shine and look at their Lord. People are not left without a purpose.
questions: What is your purpose in life?
How do you want to meet Allah on that Day?
What do you hope to see on that Day?

summary: Al-Insan means 'The Human.' Allah made people from a tiny drop to test them. He showed them the way. Some say thank you. Some do not. The good people feed the poor, the child with no parents and the prisoner. They say: 'We only do it for Allah. We want no thanks.' Allah rewards them with Paradise.
questions: Why do good people give without wanting thanks?
How can you help feed or help someone this week?
What does it mean to do something only for Allah?

summary: Al-Mursalat means 'Those Sent Out.' Allah swears by the winds. Ten times it says: 'How terrible that Day will be for those who said no!' It reminds us how we were made from a tiny drop. The earth holds the living and the dead. It asks: 'After this, what else will they believe?'
questions: Why do you think the same warning comes ten times?
How does it make you humble to know where you came from?
What can touch your heart if the Quran does not?

summary: An-Naba means 'The Big News.' It is about the Day of Judgment. Allah reminds us of what He made: the earth like a bed, mountains like pegs, sleep for rest, night like a cover, the sun like a lamp, and rain that grows gardens. Then it tells what waits for people who did wrong and for people who obeyed Allah.
questions: Which sign of Allah in the first verses do you see every day?
Why does Allah remind us of what He made before He talks about the Last Day?
What good thing do you hope to see on that Day?

summary: An-Nazi'at means 'Those Who Pull Out.' It starts with angels. It tells about the great blast on the Last Day. It tells how Allah sent Musa to Pharaoh. Pharaoh said: 'I am your highest lord.' Allah punished him. The person who fears Allah and stops himself from bad wants goes to Paradise.
questions: Why did being proud end badly for Pharaoh?
What does it mean to stop yourself from a bad want?
What is one want you need to stop right now?

summary: Abasa means 'He Frowned.' A blind man named Abdullah came to the Prophet while he was talking to important men. The Prophet frowned. Allah gently told him that the blind man wanted to learn and that was more important. Look at the food Allah grows for you. On that Day, people will run from their own family.
questions: Why is a person who really wants to learn so special?
How can you treat every person with the same respect?
Why will people run from their own family on that Day?

summary: At-Takwir means 'Rolled Up.' It lists signs of the Last Day: the sun rolls up, the stars fall, the mountains move and the seas boil. A baby girl who was buried will be asked why she was killed. The Quran is the word of a great messenger. 'So where are you going?'
questions: What does the question 'So where are you going?' make you think?
Why do you think this surah talks about the baby girl?
How can you live today so you are ready for that Day?

summary: Al-Infitar means 'Splitting Open.' The sky will split and the stars will fall. Allah asks: 'O human, what made you forget your Kind Lord, who made you and shaped you well?' Kind angels write down all you do. Good people will be in joy.
questions: What makes people forget their Lord?
How does it change you to know that kind angels write down what you do?
Why does Allah call Himself 'Kind' in this surah?

summary: Al-Mutaffifin means 'Those Who Cheat.' How terrible for those who cheat when they weigh things! They want full when they buy, but give less when they sell. Everyone will stand before Allah on the Last Day. Those who laughed at the believers will see the believers laughing at them.
questions: Why is cheating in small things also a big thing?
How can you be more honest at school, at work or at home?
What should you do when people laugh at you for doing right?

summary: Al-Inshiqaq means 'Splitting Apart.' The sky will split and the earth will flatten, and both will obey Allah. People are working hard toward their Lord and will meet Him. Some get their book in the right hand and will have an easy time. Some get it behind their back and will cry out.
questions: What does it mean that all people work toward their Lord?
How can you get ready for an easy time on that Day?
What part of life are you in now, and how can you use it well?

summary: Al-Buruj means 'The Big Stars.' It tells about believers who were burned in a ditch of fire because of their faith. Allah saw everything. Believers who do good get gardens. Allah is the Forgiving and the Loving. The Quran is safe on a Preserved Tablet.
questions: What helped the believers keep their faith?
What does it mean that Allah is the Loving?
How does it help you to know that Allah sees everything?

summary: At-Tariq means 'The Night Visitor.' Every person has an angel guard over them. Think about what you were made from: a tiny drop. Allah can bring you back to life. On that Day, secrets will be seen. The Quran is a clear word. It is not a joke.
questions: How does thinking about where you came from make you humble?
What secret do you want Allah to make clean?
Why is the Quran not a joke?

summary: Al-A'la means 'The Highest.' Praise the name of your Lord, the Highest. He made everything and shaped it, and He guides it. Whoever cleans his heart, remembers Allah and prays is a winner. People like this world more, but the next life is better and lasts forever.
questions: What does it mean to clean your heart?
Why do people like this world more than the next?
How can you remember Allah's name more during the day?

summary: Al-Ghashiyah means 'The Big Day That Covers.' Some faces will be sad and tired in a hot fire. Other faces will be happy in a high garden. Allah tells us to look at the camels, the sky, the mountains and the earth. The Prophet is a reminder. He is not a boss over people.
questions: What do you notice when you look at the sky and the mountains?
What does it mean that the Prophet is a reminder and not a boss?
How can you remind others in a gentle way?

summary: Al-Fajr means 'The Dawn.' It tells about Ad, Thamud and Pharaoh, who did bad things. People think: 'If I have a lot, Allah loves me. If I have little, Allah does not love me.' That is wrong. We must be kind to children with no parents and feed the poor. It ends with: 'O calm soul, come back to your Lord, happy and pleasing.'
questions: Does having more money mean Allah loves you more? What does the surah say?
How can you be kind to a child with no parents or to someone in need?
What does it mean to have a calm soul?

summary: Al-Balad means 'The City.' Allah swears by Makkah. People are made to work hard in life. Allah gave us eyes, a tongue and lips, and showed us two ways. The hard climb is to free a slave, to feed someone on a day of hunger, and to be kind and patient.
questions: What are the two ways Allah showed us?
How can you help someone who is hungry?
What does it mean to tell others to be patient and kind?

summary: Ash-Shams means 'The Sun.' Allah swears by the sun, moon, day, night, sky and earth. A person who cleans his heart wins. A person who spoils it loses. The people of Thamud hurt Allah's camel, so Allah destroyed them.
questions: What does it mean to clean your heart?
What habit can help you clean your heart this week?
What did the people of Thamud do that was wrong?

summary: Al-Layl means 'The Night.' People work in different ways. Whoever gives, fears Allah and believes in the good reward finds that Allah makes his way easy. Whoever is stingy and says he does not need Allah finds that the way gets hard. The best person gives only to please Allah.
questions: How does giving make life easier?
Why do you think being stingy makes life hard?
How can you give today only to please Allah?

summary: Ad-Duha means 'The Morning Light.' It cheered up the Prophet when the Quran stopped coming for a while. Allah said: 'Your Lord has not left you.' Allah took care of him when he had no parents, when he was lost, and when he was poor. So be kind to children with no parents. Do not shout at people who ask for help.
questions: How does this surah cheer up a person who feels alone?
How has Allah taken care of you in the past?
How can you be kind to someone who needs help?

summary: Ash-Sharh means 'Opening Up.' Allah cheered up the Prophet. He made his heart calm, took away his heavy load and made his name high. It says two times: 'After hard times comes ease.' When you finish one thing, work hard on the next, and turn to your Lord.
questions: What hard thing do you have now that this promise can help with?
Why do you think Allah said it two times?
What can you do after you finish a task to turn to Allah?

summary: At-Tin means 'The Fig.' Allah swears by the fig, the olive, Mount Sinai and Makkah. Allah made people in the best shape. But a person can fall very low, unless he believes and does good. Is Allah not the best of judges?
questions: What does it mean that people were made in the best shape?
How can a person fall low, and how can he stay away from that?
What does it mean to you that Allah is the best of judges?

summary: Al-Alaq means 'The Clinging Drop.' These were the first verses that came to the Prophet in the cave of Hira. Allah said: 'Read!' He taught people by the pen. He taught people what they did not know. It tells about a man who tried to stop the Prophet from praying. It ends: 'Bow down and come close to Allah.'
questions: Why do you think the first word was 'Read'?
What new thing do you want to learn this month?
How can bowing down bring a person closer to Allah?

summary: Al-Qadr means 'The Night of Power.' Allah sent down the Quran on this night. It is better than a thousand months. Angels and Jibril come down. It is full of peace until the morning. Muslims look for it in the last ten nights of Ramadan.
questions: Why do you think one night can be better than a thousand months?
What would you do if you knew tonight was the Night of Power?
How can you make the last ten nights of Ramadan special?

summary: Al-Bayyinah means 'The Clear Proof.' A clear proof came: a messenger from Allah reading clean pages. People were only told to worship Allah with an honest heart, to pray and to give. People who believe and do good are the best of all. Allah is happy with them and they are happy with Allah.
questions: What does it mean to worship Allah with an honest heart?
What makes a person the best of all: looks, money or belief and good things?
How would it feel if Allah was happy with you?

summary: Az-Zalzalah means 'The Big Shake.' On the Last Day the earth will shake and show what is inside it. People will see what they did. Even a tiny good thing will be seen. Even a tiny bad thing will be seen.
questions: What does it mean that even a tiny good thing will be seen?
What small good thing can you do today that you often skip?
What small bad habit do you want to stop?

summary: Al-Adiyat means 'The Running Horses.' Allah swears by horses running hard at dawn. Then He says that people do not say thank you to their Lord. They love money too much. On the Last Day, Allah will know what is in their hearts.
questions: In what ways can a person forget to say thank you?
How can you check if you love money too much?
What do you want Allah to find in your heart?

summary: Al-Qari'ah means 'The Great Shock.' It is the Last Day. People will be like scattered moths. Mountains will be like soft wool. People whose good deeds are heavy will be happy. People whose good deeds are light will go to a deep pit of fire.
questions: What can make your good deeds heavy?
Why are people like scattered moths on that Day?
What good thing can you add today?

summary: At-Takathur means 'Wanting More and More.' Wanting to have more and more keeps you busy until you go to the grave. Then you will know. Then you will be asked about every gift you enjoyed.
questions: What do people want more and more of today?
What gifts will you be asked about?
How can you use your gifts to please Allah?

summary: Al-Asr means 'Time.' Allah swears by time. All people are losing, except those who believe, do good, remind each other to follow the truth, and remind each other to be patient.
questions: Which one is hardest for you: believing, doing good, the truth or patience?
Who is a friend who can remind you of the truth?
How are you using your time today?

summary: Al-Humazah means 'The One Who Talks Bad About Others.' How terrible for the person who makes fun of people and talks about them behind their backs. He collects money and counts it all the time. He thinks money will make him live forever. He will be thrown into a fire called the Crusher.
questions: Why is talking bad about people so harmful?
Why can money make a person think he will live forever?
How can you use your words to help people?

summary: Al-Fil means 'The Elephant.' A king named Abraha came with an army and elephants to break down the Kaaba. This was the year the Prophet was born. Allah sent flocks of birds with small stones. His army became like chewed-up leaves. Allah protects His House.
questions: What does this story teach about Allah and big armies?
How did the Kaaba stay safe with no army?
When did you see Allah protect something in a way you did not expect?

summary: Quraysh is the name of the Prophet's tribe. They made safe trips for trade in winter and summer. So Allah says: worship the Lord of this House. He fed them when they were hungry and kept them safe from fear.
questions: What food and safety do you have to thank Allah for?
How can you show thanks to Allah with what you do?
Why should food and safety make us worship Allah?

summary: Al-Ma'un means 'Small Kindness.' Do you know who says no to the Last Day? The person who pushes away a child with no parents and does not help feed the poor. How terrible for people who pray but do not care about their prayer, who show off, and who do not even do small kind things.
questions: What small kind things can you do for others every day?
Why does Allah put prayer together with caring for people?
How can you make your prayer more honest, not for show?

summary: Al-Kawthar means 'A Great Gift.' It is the shortest surah. Allah says: 'We gave you al-Kawthar, a very big gift.' So pray to your Lord and give for Him. The one who hates you is the one who is cut off.
questions: What does a 'great gift' mean to you?
How can you say thank you to Allah when He gives you something good?
Why is it good that this surah is so short to learn?

summary: Al-Kafirun means 'Those Who Say No.' Allah tells the Prophet to say: 'I do not worship what you worship. You do not worship what I worship. You have your religion and I have mine.' It teaches us to be clear and strong about worshipping only Allah, and to live in peace with others.
questions: Why is it important to be clear about who we worship?
How can you be strong in your faith and still be kind to others?
What does 'you have your religion and I have mine' teach about respect?

summary: An-Nasr means 'The Help.' When Allah's help and the win come, and you see people joining Islam in big groups, praise your Lord and ask for His forgiveness. He is always ready to forgive. When we win, we should say thank you and not be proud.
questions: How should you act when you win or do well?
Why does Allah tell the Prophet to ask for forgiveness when he wins?
What is one good thing you want to thank Allah for?

summary: Al-Masad means 'The Rope.' It is about Abu Lahab, the Prophet's uncle, who hurt the Prophet. His wife also did bad things. His money did not help him. Being family of the Prophet does not save you. Believing and doing good is what matters.
questions: Why did being the Prophet's family not help Abu Lahab?
What does this teach about how Allah decides?
What should you trust more: your family name or what you do?

summary: Al-Ikhlas means 'Being Honest to Allah.' Allah says: 'Say: Allah is One. Allah is the one everyone needs. He has no children and was not born. No one is like Him.' It tells who Allah is in four short lines. The Prophet said it is worth one third of the Quran.
questions: What does it mean that Allah is the One everyone needs?
How is Allah different from everything He made?
How can you remember this surah in your day?

summary: Al-Falaq means 'The Daybreak.' We ask Allah to keep us safe. We ask Him to keep us safe from bad things He made, from the dark when it comes, from people who do magic, and from people who are jealous. Muslims read it with An-Nas in the morning, the evening and before sleep.
questions: What does it mean to ask Allah to keep you safe?
What can jealousy do to a heart?
How can you remember to read this surah every morning and night?

summary: An-Nas means 'People.' It is the last surah. We ask Allah, the Lord, King and God of people, to keep us safe from the whisperer. He whispers bad thoughts into hearts. He hides when we remember Allah. The whisperer can be from jinn or from people.
questions: What kinds of bad thoughts come to you?
What can you do when a bad whisper comes?
Why do you think the Quran ends with a prayer to be kept safe?
